provenance.creator: Codex agent; source-inspected and curated, not independently human-labeled
provenance.selection: One question per company, cycling source fiscal year 2021-2025; 20 narrative and 20 accepted-table questions; selected for readable source evidence. No retrieval results were used to select or rewrite questions.
limitations: Not a held-out or production-quality benchmark.
Questions are generated after inspecting the corpus, so selection and phrasing may favor lexically retrievable or clearly extracted content.
Only selected canonical evidence and listed alternatives are judged; other valid answer locations may be unjudged.
Image-only pages, rejected tables, cross-company synthesis, and open-domain or unanswerable questions are not represented.
Measures recovery of supporting source spans/rows, not answer generation accuracy.

evaluation_contract.prose: A unit is recovered when the union of source character intervals from the top 5 chunks covers [char_start,char_end) for the canonical element_id or a listed alternative. Offsets are in the original extracted element text, not normalized text.
evaluation_contract.table: A unit is recovered when a top 5 chunk contains the complete canonical table_id row_index. Canonical row key is table_id + :row: + 0-based row_index.
evaluation_contract.per_question_recall: Recovered required evidence units divided by number of required evidence units; alternatives do not add denominator units.
evaluation_contract.aggregate: Macro-average the per-question evidence Recall@5; separately report all-required-evidence success and prose/table subsets.
evaluation_contract.fixed_controls: Use identical questions, corpus, tokenizer, retriever, ranking settings, and top-k across chunking groups. Do not index reference answers, quotes, or other benchmark labels.

validation.source_identity: All 48 required units validated against the corresponding parsed element or accepted table row with document and source hash identity.
validation.native_pdf_text: All 23 narrative evidence quotes also matched whitespace-normalized text extracted directly from their raw-PDF bounding boxes.
validation.table_check: All 25 selected table rows were compared with native raw-PDF row text; year-column headers and contextual units were inspected.

questions.question: According to ServiceNow's FY2024 annual report, why can a slowdown in new or renewed subscriptions take time to affect ServiceNow's reported revenue?

evidence.quote: We generally recognize revenues from customers ratably over the terms of their subscriptions. Net new annual contract value from new subscriptions and expansion contracts entered into during a period can generally be expected to generate revenues for the duration of the subscription term. As a result, a significant portion of the revenues we report in each period are derived from the recognition of deferred revenues relating to subscriptions entered into during previous periods.

Consequently, a decrease in new or renewed subscriptions, expansion contracts in any single reporting period will have a limited impact on our revenues for that period, but they will negatively affect our operating results in future periods.

questions.reference_answer: Subscription revenue is recognized ratably over the subscription term, so reported revenue includes deferred revenue from earlier contracts. Fewer new or renewed subscriptions have limited current-period impact but hurt future results.

questions.question: According to Autodesk's FY2025 annual report, what does Autodesk mean by unbilled deferred revenue, and is that balance recorded as a receivable or deferred revenue under ASC 606?

evidence.quote: Unbilled Deferred Revenue: Unbilled deferred revenue represents contractually stated or committed orders under early renewal and multi-year billing plans for subscription, services, and maintenance for which the associated deferred revenue has not been recognized. Under FASB Accounting Standards Codification ("ASC") Topic 606, unbilled deferred revenue is not included as a receivable or deferred revenue on our Consolidated Balance Sheet.

questions.reference_answer: It represents contractually stated or committed orders under early-renewal and multi-year billing plans whose associated deferred revenue has not been recognized. Under ASC 606 it is not recorded as either a receivable or deferred revenue on the consolidated balance sheet.
